evidence: Sall. Jug. 92.3: pauca repugnantibus Numidīs capit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The general word: a town, a camp, a ship is capta however it fell.
To take by assault, as opposed to oppugnāre, to attack (see attack): Caesar attacked Noviodunum on the march expugnāre nōn potuit, but could not take it.

terms.gloss: gain possession of, become master of
terms.grammar: verb, fourth conjugation, deponent, with the ablative
terms.comment: With the ablative (oppidō potīrī); of anything one gets hold of, not only places.

phrases.latin: id ex itinere oppugnāre cōnātus, expugnāre nōn potuit
phrases.english: he tried to attack it on the march, but could not take it

sources: Lewis & Short: capio · Lewis & Short: expugno · Lewis & Short: potior
